rows.authors: Juan Carlos Gómez Alonso; Sergio Segura; Antonio Ruiz–Cortés
rows.abstract: Test case generation tools for REST APIs have grown in number and complexity in recent years. However, their advanced capabilities for automated input generation contrast with the simplicity of their test oracles, which limit the types of failures they can detect to crashes, regressions, and violations of the API specification or design best practices. In this paper, we present AGORA, an approach for the automated generation of test oracles for REST APIs through the detection of invariants—properties of the output that should always hold. rows.authors: Juan Carlos Gómez Alonso; Michael D. Ernst; Sergio Segura; Antonio Ruiz–Cortés

rows.title: SATORI: Static Test Oracle Generation for REST APIs
rows.venue: IEEE/ACM International Conference on Automated Software Engineering (ASE)
rows.authors: Juan Carlos Gómez Alonso; Alberto Martin-Lopez; Sergio Segura; Gabriele Bavota
rows.abstract: REST API test case generation tools are evolving rapidly, with growing capabilities for the automated generation of complex tests. However, despite their strengths in test data generation, these tools are constrained by the types of test oracles they support, often limited to crashes, regressions, and noncompliance with API specifications or design standards. This paper introduces SATORI (Static API Test ORacle Inference), a black-box approach for generating test oracles for REST APIs by analyzing their OpenAPI Specification. rows.title: Test Oracle Generation for REST APIs—RCR Report
rows.venue: ACM Transactions on Software Engineering and Methodology
rows.authors: Juan Carlos Gómez Alonso; Michael D. Ernst; Sergio Segura; Antonio Ruiz–Cortés
rows.abstract: This Replicated Computational Results (RCR) Report accompanies our TOSEM article “Test Oracle Generation for REST APIs.” In this work we introduce AGORA+, a black-box approach for automatically generating domain-specific test oracles for REST APIs by detecting invariants—output properties that should always hold. As part of this RCR, we provide a replication package (available at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.12506791 ) that enables the full reproduction of our results and is designed to pave the way for future research.

rows.title: RESTOR: Automated Test Oracle Generation for RESTful APIs via Reinforcement Learning
rows.venue: Proceedings of the ACM on software engineering.
rows.authors: Xun Zhou; Zhen Dong; Mingyu Ren; Qiang Li
rows.abstract: Modern REST API testing faces a critical challenge in defining reliable test oracles, particularly in agile industrial environments where formal specifications (e.g., OpenAPI) are frequently missing or outdated, and historical execution logs are unavailable for newly deployed endpoints. In this paper, we present RESTOR (Reinforcement Enhanced Single-Traffic Oracle generator for REST APIs), a framework that generates executable test assertions from a single observed request-response pair in a black-box setting. rows.venue: IEEE Annual Computers, Software, and Applications Conference (COMPSAC)
rows.authors: Shehroz Khan; Abdullah Mughees; Gaadha Sudheerbabu; Tanwir Ahmad
rows.abstract: As REST APIs become an increasingly significant part of software systems, their validation is becoming more critical. Hence, testing and uncovering underlying issues are of utmost importance for improving software quality. However, testing REST APIs is challenging mainly due to the difficulty of assessing whether the output of an API call is correct, i.e., the test oracle problem. rows.title: Fuzzing for Detecting Access Policy Violations in REST APIs
rows.venue: IEEE International Symposium on Software Reliability Engineering (ISSRE)
rows.authors: Andrea Arcuri; Omur Sahin; Man Zhang
rows.abstract: Due to their widespread use in industry, several techniques have been proposed in the literature to fuzz REST APIs. rows.title: Automated black‐box testing of nominal and error scenarios in RESTful APIs
rows.authors: Davide Corradini; Amedeo Zampieri; Michele Pasqua; Emanuele Viglianisi
rows.abstract: Abstract RESTful APIs (or REST APIs for short) represent a mainstream approach to design and develop web APIs using the REpresentational State Transfer architectural style. Black‐box testing, which assumes only the access to the system under test with a specific interface, is the only viable option when white‐box testing is impracticable. rows.title: Automated test generation for REST APIs: no time to rest yet
rows.venue: ACM SIGSOFT International Symposium on Software Testing and Analysis (ISSTA)
rows.authors: Myeong‐Soo Kim; Xin Qi; Saurabh Kumar Sinha; Alessandro Orso
rows.abstract: Modern web services routinely provide REST APIs for clients to access their functionality. These APIs present unique challenges and opportunities for automated testing, driving the recent development of many techniques and tools that generate test cases for API endpoints using various strategies. Understanding how these techniques compare to one another is difficult, as they have been evaluated on different benchmarks and using different metrics. rows.title: FDRRestTest: Feedback-Driven Logical Testing for REST APIs
rows.venue: DROPS (Schloss Dagstuhl – Leibniz Center for Informatics)
rows.abstract: Background. REST APIs have become the primary interaction interface for modern software systems, making automated black-box API testing increasingly important. However, existing testing techniques still face three major limitations: over-reliance on dependencies extracted from static specifications, failure to fully utilise failed requests as feedback, and an overemphasis on crash-oriented verification, resulting in insufficient exploration of non-crash-prone logical defects. rows.title: Validating HTTP Semantics in REST APIs With Constructed Call Sequence Scenarios
rows.abstract: Context: REST APIs are widely used in industry. These APIs use HTTP for their communications. Failures in following the specifications of HTTP can lead to confusing and hard to use APIs, with possibly serious software faults with dire consequences. Objectives: Define novel automated techniques to automatically find HTTP semantics-level faults in existing REST APIs.
